title: Finance and Corporate Services Committee - November 24, 2025

items.title: Commencement
notes: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee held a meeting this date commencing at 10:05 a.m.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
Councillor P. Singh - Capital Forecast & Issue Papers
Councillor S. Stretch - Kitchener Public Library (KPL)
Councillor M. Johnston - Capital Forecast & Issue Papers
Councillor D. Chapman - Capital Forecast & Issue Papers
General Overview by the Chief Financial Officer
notes:
J. Lautenbach provided opening remarks on the 2026 Budget, including an overview of the City's Budget process. J. Lautenbach stated for the 2026 Budget, staff would be providing a presentation on the Operating and Capital Budget this date, which would be followed by the Mayor formally tabling the Budget on December 1, 2025, and Final Budget Day on December 11, 2025.  J. Lautenbach noted Council previously considered Financial Services Department report FIN-2025-408, which shortened the budget window as per Strong Mayor's Legislation, noting as per that approval, the 2026 is proposed to be adopted on December 26, 2026.

Councillor B. Ioannidis entered the meeting at this time.

J. Lautenbach highlighted inflationary pressures and economic trends and responses, stating the 2026 budget theme is defined as "Affordable Today and Ready for Tomorrow". The themes include an emphasis on affordable city services; smart investments in infrastructure and focusing on the future. J. Lautenbach stated Kitchener’s proposed property tax increase and water utilities increase combined represents an impact of less than $10 per month for the average household, which includes an average household impact of 2.2% (approximately $29.) for property taxes and a water utilities increase of 6.3% (approximately $88.) for a total annual impact of $117. J. Lautenbach shared the 10-year Capital forecast includes over $1B in planned spending to take care of critical underground infrastructure and highlighted some of those investments including but not limited to the City’s Water Infrastructure Program (WIP); and, the Cowan Recreation Centre scheduled to open in 2026. J. Lautenbach stated Grant funding continues to be an important funding source to advance capital priorities, indicating the City has secured $200M in grant funding over the past 5 years. J. Lautenbach shared a Regional comparison for the cumulative tax rate increases, noting the City has had the lowest average increase of 3.7% over the last 5-years. J. Lautenbach finally advised the 2026 budget continues the longstanding trend of Kitchener delivering affordable city services to its residents and businesses. It also makes smart investments in infrastructure that will renew existing assets as well as create new ones, commenting all of this makes sure Kitchener is Affordable Today, Ready for Tomorrow.

items.title: Centre in the Square (CITS)
notes:
E. Lariviere, Executive Director and D. Carli, Board Chair, Centre in the Square (CITS) were in attendance to provide an overview of the 2026 CITS budget and to respond to questions from the Committee.

D. Carli highlighted the state of the 2025 activities and budget, including increases in programming and summer camp resulting in a small surplus, 50th anniversary celebration events planned in 2030 and development of a new strategic plan. The 2026 budget includes an operating grant increase of 2.5% as per City guidelines, from $2.138M to $2.191M. D. Carli stated the 2026 new investment is aligned with the 4 pillars of growth strategy: destination, community engagement, capacity building, and branding.

D. Carli then responded to questions from Committee on diversification of programming, and recent surplus distribution process changes to assist with capital replacement projects. E. Lariviere responded to questions regarding the overall performance revenue projections in 2026, use of the studio theatre, the projected budget shortfall for 2025, comparative performance centers that are solely funded by the municipality, and the revival of the Kitchener Waterloo Symphony. 

Councillor P. Singh left and returned to the meeting at this time. 

Councillor B. Ioannidis left and returned to the meeting at this time.

Sustainability of broadway shows and programming, and partnership with the Creative Industries area at the city was discussed. E. Lariviere responded to questions from Council regarding challenges with operating the current facility.

items.title: Kitchener Public Library (KPL)
notes:
D. Solomon, Kitchener Public Library (KPL) was in attendance to provide an overview of the 2026 Budget and highlighted recent transition planning for the new service model being implemented out of the KPL's new Strategic Plan and 2025 successes including the community library locker service and potential to expand the program once the pilot ends into three areas including Bridgeport, Centreville Chicopee and Huron South.

D. Solomon and L. Lawrence then responded to questions from Committee regarding visitor and programming data, funding from other levels of government and advocacy efforts, borrowing collection for technological devices, and communication practices, outreach and capital costs required for the library locker service. The collection and use of data for data-driven decision making and planned enhancements was highlighted by D. Solomon.  A. Riddell, L. Lee, and K. Johnson-Perlock, were also in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee.

items.title: Tax Supported Operating Budget
notes:
R. Hagey provided an overview of the proposed tax rate increase of 2.2%, noting the proposed increase not only supports the operating needs for the continued delivery of programs and services, but also addresses operating budget growth-related pressures, including incorporating the full operating costs for the new Cowan Recreation Centre which represented a 0.9% tax related impact on its own.

R. Hagey further advised the proposed tax rate increase, including utility rate increases, are anticipated to have an $117 Impact on the average household in 2026. R. Hagey noted the 2025 user fees are increasing by 4%, which is in line with inflation, and the complete user fee schedule can be found in Appendix E. 

R. Hagey confirmed the City collects all of the property taxes for itself, the Region and local School Board. Further, the City’s portion of the tax bill is 30%, with the Region of Waterloo and the local School Boards making up 58% and 12% respectively. 

R. Hagey then responded to questions from Committee on new assessment growth and user fees.

D. Saunderson, J. Lautenbach, J. Readman, B. Cheyne, D. Chapman and D. McGoldrick, then responded to questions regarding proposed user fees.

Councillor M. Johnston left and returned to the meeting at this time. 

In response to a question from Committee, D. McGoldrick addressed proposed user fees related to the Public Tree By-law, approved by Council earlier this year and J Readman noted that the Private Tree By-law is expected to come forward to Council in early 2026.

G. McNeil responded to questions regarding recovering costs for by-law enforcement charges as the city continues to grow, addressed processes related to repeated enforcement complaints and the use of technology to address potential property standards violations.

Councillor A. Owodunni left the meeting at this time.

items.title: Recess and Reconvene
notes: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee then recessed at 12:21 p.m. and reconvened at 1:11 p.m., Chaired by Councillor S. Davey, with all members present, Councillor A. Owodunni was participating virtually.

items.title: Enterprise Operating Budgets
notes:
R. Hagey provided an overview of the City’s enterprises, noting enterprises are self-sufficient business lines that raise their own revenues through user rates instead of being funded through property taxes. The 7 enterprises include: building, golf, parking, water sanitary, stormwater and gas. 

R. Hagey then provided an overview of each of the 7 enterprises and their 2026 operating budgets, which included a budget and 5-year forecast. R. Hagey advised that the combined annual Water Infrastructure Program (WIP) rate has an increase of 6.3% over next three years to fund planned workplan.

items.title: Building Enterprise Budget
notes: R. Hagey provided an overview of the Building Enterprise budget. There were no questions from Committee.

items.title: Golf Enterprise Budget
notes:
Councillor A. Owodunni re-entered the meeting at this time.

R. Hagey provided an overview of the Golf Enterprise Budget. B. Cheyne, R. Hagey and D. Chapman were in attendance to respond to questions related to the 2025 Golf Season and the increased use of the golf courses, as well as the dividend transfers, the potential to pay off debt sooner and clarification on the Golf Reserve Fund. Questions were also raised about whether the golf courses were considered for sponsorship opportunities.

Councillor J. Deneault and B. Ioannidis left the meeting at this time.

Councillor J. Deneault re-entered the meeting at this time.

items.title: Parking Enterprise Budget
notes:
R. Hagey provided an overview of the Parking Enterprise Budget. J. Readman was in attendance to respond to questions related to the parking enterprise budget, noting the budget is based on the user fee structure.

Councillor B. Ioannidis re-entered the meeting at this time. 

In response to further questions related to parking in the Downtown, it was noted staff are currently reviewing office rate vacancies in the Downtown and it is anticipated that work will be brought forward to Council sometime in 2026. J. Readman further advised gate revenue has increased due to special event parking from the CITS and some return to work within the downtown, as well as an uptake on some parking revenue due to the parking lease with the Hospital of the Bramm Street lot.

items.title: Utilities Overview - Water Utility, Sanitary Utility and Stormwater Utility Budgets
notes:
Councillor A. Owodunni left the meeting and re-entered at this time.

R. Hagey provided an overview of the Water Utility, Sanitary Utility and Stormwater Utility Budgets. There were no questions from the Committee.

items.title: Gas Utility
notes: R. Hagey provided an overview of the Gas Utility. G. St. Louis and D. McGoldrick responded to questions, related to gas line infrastructure replacements, growth of the utility and the non-regulated programs including rental water heaters. In response to further questions, J. Lautenbach responded to questions about the dividend transfer to the City, noting the allocation was frozen, as its amount was determined to be too high as per the Ontario Energy Board (OEB) regulation requirements.

items.title: Capital Budget Overview
notes: R. Hagey presented an overview of the capital priority setting process and high-level capital budget summary, noting the capital budget includes more than 400 projects with a total cost of $1.8 billion over 10 years, with $201 million of spending in the first year, which includes investment in items including but not limited to: This includes an additional Fire Truck ($1.5M in 2026); Community Trail Improvements ($1.7M in 2026, $39.9M overall in the capital forecast); Tree Planting ($3.3M in 2026, $8.2M overall in the capital forecast); and, Middle Strasburg Creek Naturalization ($4.3M in 2026).

items.title: Strategic Addition
notes:
R. Hagey, Director, Financial Planning, addressed Committee related to strategic addition funding, noting there is $1M of one-time funding available to Council for allocation to priority areas. R. Hagey stated staff have identified four potential areas where funds could be invested, but Council could direct them somewhere else. R. Hagey further advised more details about each of the options provided in the issue paper in Appendix G (p10-11).

Questions were raised about the possibility of funding an additional library lockers from the funding, noting the lockers have a purchase price of $50,000, that if it was Council's will, it could be installed at Kingsdale and Centreville Chicopee Community Centres. D. Chapman noted Council could opt to provide that additional funding to the Library, but it would be the Library that would have control on how the funding is allocated. D. Chapman further advised they would also need to confirm that they have staffing resources to manage the additional boxes through their operating. D. Chapman stated the Library expressed interest in piloting the program for one more year just to confirm the full uptake of the program.

Councillor P. Singh left the meeting at this time.

Council then further discussed the proposed strategic options, including more specific improvements related to community bbq pits, park/playground improvements and/or amenities; as well as, special event proposals and/or supplies for 2026.

Councillor P. Singh re-entered the meeting at this time.

The business retention program was also expressed as an area of interest.

items.title: Capital Funding Sources
notes:
R. Hagey reported the funding sources for the ten-year forecast of the Capital budget. R. Hagey noted that more half of the capital budget funding comes from the City’s self-funded operations or enterprises at 64% (Building, Golf, Parking, Water, Sanitary, Storm & Gas); Development charges (DCs) at 10%, the Capital Pool at 10%, and all other sources under 10%. R. Hagey further advised the change in funding sources from year to year Capital pool is down $16.7m because  some items were moved from capital over to the operating budget and DCs revenues are decreased by $99M.  R. Hagey further advised, the capital pool is once again fully balanced in all years of the capital forecast, which means the city will have an actual funding plan for all of those projects in the forecast.

Councillor S. Stretch left and re-entered the meeting at this time.

items.title: Debt
notes: R. Hagey reviewed the City's outstanding debt and noted the City's debt levels have been decreasing for the past decade, but will see increasing debt in order to fund growth-related infrastructure needed as the city continues to grow. R. Hagey stated City debt terms, like the length of the debt or interest rates, cannot be renegotiated once the debt is issued. R. Hagey further advised the City needs to issue Development Charges (DC) debt to fund some large dollar growth related projects like the Cowan Recreation Centre and some roads & sewer infrastructure.

items.title: Reserve Funds
notes:
R. Hagey spoke to Reserve Fund balances, and the ratings and projections for each fund category. R. Hagey noted the reserve levels are positive, indicating the City has a long-standing reserve fund policy, and the key principles of the policy include: only using reserve funds for their intended purpose; maintaining positive balances in all reserve funds; and, setting minimum targets for reserves. R. Hagey noted reserve funds are grouped into 5 Council approved categories, including: Stabilization, Corporate, Program Specific, Capital and Obligatory, and provided an overview of each of the categories. R. Hagey, J. Lautenbach and D. Chapman then responded to questions from the Committee.

Councillor P. Singh left the meeting at this time.

items.title: Development Charges
notes:
R. Hagey stated the basic idea of Development Charges (DC) is that growth should pay for growth, and the costs of new infrastructure should not be borne by existing taxpayers. R. Hagey stated there has been a lot of legislative change to DCs recently, which generally have had a negative impact on DC cashflows to municipalities, including but not limited to: additional exemptions and mandatory reductions and later payments. R. Hagey indicated the current DC by-law was approved in 2022 and runs until mid-2027, noting staff are planning to come back to Council in spring 2026 to get direction on how to proceed, indicating the need to possibility of start a new by-law, or possibly extending the term of the existing bylaw. R. Hagey then responded to questions from Committee.

Councillor P. Singh re-entered the meeting at this time.

Councillor D. Schnider left and re-entered the meeting at this time.

items.title: Capital Budget Content
notes: R. Hagey introduced the Capital Budget portion of the budget materials, noting the balance of the package includes the capital forecast and investment options, issue papers and the quality of fund estimates. R. Hagey highlighted the budget has a couple differences, some capital lines have been moved over to divisional operating budgets, because they are more operating in nature, indicating moving them reduces adjustments that have been needed to prepare our audited financial statements; and, the 1st year of funding for General Provision accounts has been broken out as their own project which keeps funds organized so the city can track usage more easily. R. Hagey then provided an overview on the terms and definitions to help clarify how the definition terms within the capital budget.

items.title: Capital Forecast & Issue Papers
notes:
The Committee reviewed the Capital Forecast outlined in Appendix C and the Issue Papers in Appendix G of the budget package.

Staff responded to questions related to the funding for winter ice rinks, and heritage grant funding. B. Gilmore and J. Lautenbach were in attendance to respond to questions related to Procurement Equipment - PPE Suppliers.

J. Readman was in attendance to respond to questions related to traffic calming initiatives. J. Readman stated it is anticipated in 2026 that there will be additional provincial funding coming that may assist with helping to expand the flexi sign program. J. Readman further advised, in addition to the procurement increases, there are additional staffing implications related to the program that would also need to be addressed if the program was expanded beyond its current capacity. J. Readman agreed to recirculate a previous issue paper on the flexi-sign program.

items.title: Additional Budget Matters
notes:
The Chair noted that was the end of the formal budget presentation and questioned the Committee if they had any further comments to raise prior to adjournment.

Questions and response were received related to the approved asset management plan and the new Regional Garbage Collection program.

Questions were raised regarding staff’s report back on a proposed renoviction by-law and whether there was funding in the 2026 budget to accommodate that program. V. Raab responded to questions, noting there is no funding currently allocated in the 2026 budget, stating staff are still in the process of completing that work and are not able to speak to the potential resources that may be required to facilitate such a program. V. Raab indicated that information will be included with the report back, once completed.

Further questions were raised regarding washroom facilities at McLennan Park. D. McGoldrick responded to questions from Committee, noting staff are actively working towards finding a more suitable solution at this time.

items.title: Adjournment
notes:
On motion, this meeting adjourned at 3:49 p.m.

 

Dianna Saunderson

Manager of Council/Committee Services & Deputy Clerk

 

Amanda Fusco

Director, Legislated Services & City Clerk
